newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Amnesty asks EU to pressure Algeria on human rights.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty asks EU to pressure Algeria on human rights.

text.p: The European Union should use planned talks on trade with Algeria to pressure the country to improve its human rights record, Amnesty International Secretary General Pierre Sane said on Tuesday.

"The negotiations can be used to take concrete steps...the Algerian government should say what it is doing to end torture...and agree to legitimise the work of human rights groups in Algeria," Sane told a news conference on a report on alleged human rights abuses in Algeria.
At least 50,000 people have died since the Algerian army annulled 1992 elections in the North African nation which islamic parties looked set to win, the report said.
"Extrajudicial executions, deliberate and arbitrary killings, 'disappearances', torture, abductions, death threats have become part of Algeria's daily reality," it said.
The EU and 11 Mediterranean countries, including Algeria, agreed last November to move towards free trade in industrial goods through a series of separately negotiated trade accords.
Each planned agreement includes a clause referring to the safeguard of human rights. The agreements also foresee cooperation in other areas.

Sane said there was no reason why the EU, which is now dependent on Algeria for a large portion of its natural gas supplies, should not use its economic clout to try and influence the country's government.
"The two issues are not incompatible. The EU can get its gas from Algeria and at the same time tell Algeria it is unhappy with the human rights situation," Sane said.
"If the EU shows it is only concerned about Algerian gas what will the Algerian people think?" he added.
The 45-page report entitled "Algeria: Fear and Silence" published on Tuesday is Amnesty's sixth into allegations of human rights abuses in Algeria since 1993, Sane said.
